key_insight: A compact pediatric foundation model, TEDDY, can forecast future disease risk and visit timing from longitudinal ICD-coded histories across many diagnoses, including rare conditions.
clinical_relevance: This suggests routine pediatric EHR diagnosis histories may help identify children at elevated risk earlier, potentially supporting broader risk stratification without requiring massive model sizes.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Modeled longitudinal diagnosis trajectories and visit timing using only prior information before the target visit.
Evaluated 797 onset-prediction tasks against sex- and age-matched controls and compared with CNN, RNN, LSTM, DenseNet, and a large language model baseline.
evidence_signal: TEDDY achieved a median AUC of 72.0% across 797 disease-onset tasks, with strong performance on rare diagnoses and benchmark AUCs of 79.3% for asthma and 84.7% for ADHD.
watch_item: This was trained and tested at a single pediatric institution, and visit-timing calibration remained imperfect for median and long-tail return intervals.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
